title: When research assessment exercises leave room for opportunistic behavior by the subjects under evaluation
reasoning: The paper explicitly discusses 'opportunistic behavior,' 'perverse effects,' 'scientific misconduct,' 'plagiarism,' 'self-plagiarism,' 'scientific fraud,' 'favoritism,' and 'nepotism' as outcomes of research assessment systems. It evaluates the occurrence and context of these moral and ethical issues related to research conduct.
